fields.h1: Build a Coaching Landing Page That Finds the Right Clients
fields.hero_description: Get a coaching landing page from one prompt, with every call request and signup saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for Your Coaching Offer
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the page a prospective client reads, the form they fill in, and the table where every request waits for your reply.
fields.feature_1:
Your offer, written into a page

Describe who you coach and the change you help them make. Emergent builds the page around it: the offer, your approach, client stories, and a request form. Prompt to change it.
fields.feature_2:
Questions before the first call

Add the questions you would ask on a first call, such as role or team size. The app uses the answers to decide what each visitor sees next. Calls then go to people you can help.
fields.feature_3:
Every request kept in one table

The app saves each request and signup to a database you own, with the visitor's answers beside their name. Sort by date or answer to see who still waits for a reply.
fields.feature_4:
Word the moment someone applies

Name how you want to hear about new requests, and the app sends an email, Slack message, or in-app alert with the answers. A reminder follows if a request sits unanswered.
fields.feature_5:
New clients land in your CRM

The app connects to any tool with an API, HubSpot among them. A new request arrives in your CRM with its answers attached, and nobody retypes details from an inbox by hand.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Publish on your own domain, such as yourname.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Only applicants who lead 5 or more people reach the call

Mireille Osei asks each applicant their role, team size, and goal. Those who lead 5 or more people reach her call request, and the app emails her each one; the rest are offered her group program. In September 22 of 31 applicants reached the call request, Tobiah Strand among them, and 9 were offered the group program.
fields.tab_content_2:
Kestrin turns 8 managers into a 48-session plan

An HR lead buying coaching for managers tells Kestrin Leadership's page how many need coaching and how many sessions each. The app multiplies them into a total and adds the request to HubSpot as a deal. Saoirse Vantongeren at Quenby Foods entered 8 managers at 6 sessions each: a 48-session plan.
fields.tab_content_3:
All 12 seats taken and 9 names on the waitlist

Hollis Marchetti's group program for first-time managers has 12 seats, and the page shows how many are left. Once all 12 are taken, the signup form becomes a waitlist that keeps each person's place in line. The spring group filled in 11 days, and 9 people have joined the waitlist since, Tamsin Achterberg first.
fields.tab_content_4:
When a manager scores under 24, a call invite goes out

Nordale Sales Coaching's scorecard asks sales managers to rate 8 statements from 1 to 5. The page shows a score out of 40, saves it with the manager's email, and invites anyone under 24 to book a call. In August 64 managers took it and 26 scored under 24. Joaquin Ferreira scored 21.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Coaching Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a coaching landing page from one ideal client to a live page that sorts every call request.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one client you most want more of: their role, the problem they bring, and what changes for them by the end. Every section of the page speaks to that person.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open on the outcome in your client's words, such as running a weekly team meeting that ends on time. Your method and credentials sit lower, for readers who want to know how.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask two or three past clients for a short quote and permission to use their first name and role. A specific quote about one change reads stronger than general praise.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose one action for the page: a call request, a group signup, or a scorecard. Two competing buttons split the readers who were ready to act.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your offer into Emergent with the questions you want answered before a call. Emergent builds the page and a table that keeps every answer, ready for your first test.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide who answers each request, even if that is only you, and how fast. A prospective client who asked for a call should hear back the same working day.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send yourself a test request, check that the row lands in your table and the alert arrives, then publish on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits) and share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is a coaching landing page?
faq_plan.a: A coaching landing page is a single page that sells one coaching offer to one kind of client and asks for one step, such as a discovery call request. It names who the coaching is for, the change it helps them make, how the work runs, and what past clients say. Unlike a full coaching website, it has no menu that leads the reader away from that step.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a coaching landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe your offer, the client it serves, and the step you want them to take in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. Emergent builds the page and the database each request is saved to. Before you start, collect a few client quotes you have permission to use. Then send yourself a test request and publish.

faq_plan.q: What do the best coaching landing page examples have in common?
faq_plan.a: The best coaching landing page examples name a specific client in the headline, such as new managers or founders hiring their first team. They describe one outcome that client can picture, quote a past client by first name and role, and ask for one step. Judge each example by its first screen: if it does not say who the coach serves, skip that pattern.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a designer to make a coaching landing page?
faq_plan.a: No. A coaching page wins on clear words about who you help, and a plain layout carries those words well. A design agency landing page has to show its craft on the page itself; yours has to show you understand the client. Emergent builds the layout from a plain-English prompt, and you change any section by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: Does a coaching landing page need to list prices?
faq_plan.a: Only when the offer is fixed, such as a group program or a set number of sessions. Then people who request a call already know what it costs. Leave the price off when every engagement is scoped on a call, and say that plainly next to the button, for example: packages are set after a short call about your goals. A page that hides the price without a reason leaves visitors guessing.

faq_plan.q: What should a coach landing page ask before someone books a call?
faq_plan.a: Ask what they want to change, why now, and what they have already tried. Those answers tell you whether you can help before the call starts, and they give you a first question to open with. Keep the form to five questions or fewer, and make only the ones you act on required. On a page Emergent builds, the answers sit in a database you own, beside each person's name.

faq_plan.q: How narrow should the audience be on a coaching landing page?
faq_plan.a: Narrow enough that a reader sees themselves in the headline: for first-time engineering managers reads as meant for them, while for leaders reads as meant for anyone. Use your clients' own words for their work, too. If you coach the heads of charities, write about boards, donors, and program staff, the words a nonprofit landing page uses with its own readers.

faq_plan.q: How do I quote clients on a coaching landing page without breaking confidentiality?
faq_plan.a: Ask each client for written permission, and show them the exact quote and how their name will appear before it goes live. A first name and a role make a quote credible without naming their employer. Leave out details about colleagues or the problems discussed in sessions unless the client agrees, and take a quote down whenever a client asks.

faq_plan.q: What call to action works best on a coaching landing page?
faq_plan.a: A discovery call request works best for one-to-one and team coaching, because those engagements are scoped in conversation. For a fixed group program, a direct signup skips a call nobody needs. Word the button as what happens next, such as Request a 20-minute call, not Submit. Put a single line under it about when you will reply.

faq_plan.q: Can one coaching landing page cover several coaching services?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the services share a buyer and a next step. Split them when they do not: a team package bought by HR and a group program joined by individual managers need different headlines and forms. Link the separate pages from one page that lists every service, which works like a category landing page for your practice.

plan.angle: Searchers for a coaching landing page want examples and a quick way to get a page that turns a reader into a paying client. The top results stop at layouts and screenshots. This page shows four coaching pages built from a prompt and what each one does with a visitor: an executive coach's page that asks 3 questions before the call request, a leadership firm's page that turns an HR lead's manager count into a session plan, a group program that switches to a waitlist when its 12 seats are taken, and a sales coach's scorecard that invites low scorers to a call. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, what strong examples share, design, prices, screening questions, niche focus, testimonials and confidentiality, the call to action, and one page per service. Course pages and personal pages are siblings and stay out; no health, wellness or money coaching niches.
